title: SCHOOL Has One O? Roster Form Explained Simply | PUC Maths Class 11
description:
Spell SCHOOL: six letters, S, C, H, O, O, L. Now write the set of its letters: only five. Where did the second O go? In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Maths (NCERT Chapter 1, Sets) we learn the two ways of writing a set, roster form and set builder form, and how to switch between them.

You will watch the letters of SCHOOL drop into a set live, with the repeated O bouncing off, see why order never matters (TEA and ATE are different words but the same set), test x one value at a time to turn a set builder rule into a roster list, and find the rule hiding behind 1, 4, 9, 16, ... There are two pause-and-think questions, a worked example with the fractions 1/2 to 6/7, the COMMITTEE exam trap, an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11 and JEE Main students.

In this video:
0:00 SCHOOL: six letters, five elements
0:25 Rule 1: no element is written twice (live)
1:09 Rule 2: order does not matter
1:43 Set builder to roster: test x live
2:29 Roster to set builder: find the rule
3:07 x is the element, n is only a counter
3:43 Worked example: 1/2, 2/3, ... 6/7
4:17 Exam trap: letters of COMMITTEE
4:33 Where it is asked
4:44 Practice question (JEE Main pattern)
5:19 Recap and three questions to answer

Next episode (Ep 4): Empty, Finite, Infinite and Universal Sets. The set of even primes bigger than 2: is it nothing, or something?

Video by Quest Academy.
